summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of morbid obesity, obstructive sleep apnea, COPD, chronic diastolic heart failure, and tobacco use was admitted for lethargy and hypoxia. She had been increasingly somnolent and was found with low oxygen levels, improving with supplemental oxygen. Chest imaging showed moderate pulmonary edema contributing to her respiratory compromise, and she was treated with IV furosemide. She remained noncompliant with CPAP use during admission and declined smoking cessation. Her metabolic encephalopathy improved with supportive care. She was discharged home with services, on unchanged medications, with strong recommendations to use CPAP and stop smoking to reduce readmission risk.
